chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from Abu Ismail, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you! The Shias in our presence are numerous.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'So do the rich show kindness to the poor, and do the righteous overlook the faults of the sinners, and do they help each other?' I said, 'No.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Those are not Shias. The Shia is the one who does this.'
ai.seo_question: What are the defining ethical characteristics of a true Shia according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) redefines Shiahood as a qualitative state of ethical conduct rather than a mere demographic or titular identity, emphasizing social solidarity through financial generosity, forgiveness, and mutual aid. This definition aligns with the Shia scholarly tradition of 'Shi'a al-Mu'minin' (Partisans of the Believers), where adherence to the Ahl al-Bayt is demonstrated through practical implementation of their moral teachings in communal life. The narration serves as a critical criterion for distinguishing true followers from nominal ones, highlighting that the essence of the sect lies in its social ethics.
